en.heading: 1 June: remembering Korea's Righteous Armies
en.origin: Righteous Armies Remembrance Day honours volunteer fighters, known in Korea as uibyeong, who resisted threats to Korean sovereignty during different periods of the country's history. The present South Korean government observance highlights their self-sacrifice and a commitment to preserving historical remembrance. The original militias existed long before a modern national commemorative calendar. On 25 May 2010 the government formally designated 1 June a statutory remembrance day. The legal date does not imply that the earliest Righteous Armies were first formed on 1 June 2010. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.

en.heading: 15 October: the Korean sports day changed its name in 2023
en.origin: South Korea's Sports Day promotes physical activity, access to sport and healthy use of leisure time. Its legal background includes the National Sports Promotion Act of 1962. A regulatory change on 10 July 2023 renamed the occasion Sports Day. The 1969 founding of the earlier day and the 2023 renaming are different milestones, not two separate sports festivals. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.

en.heading: 8 October: Korea's Veterans Association Day changed its anniversary
en.origin: Veterans Association Day recognizes former military personnel and the work of veterans' associations in South Korea. The national association was established in Busan on 1 February 1952. After organizational changes during the 1950s and membership in an international veterans federation in 1961, the government designated a Veterans Association Day on 8 June 1965, originally linked to 8 May. On 30 March 1973 it became a statutory commemoration, and on 19 June 2002 the government moved it from 8 May to 8 October. The association's founding and the modern date are distinct. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.

en.heading: 5 October: World Koreans Day connects overseas communities
en.origin: World Koreans Day recognizes Korean communities living abroad and their ties with the Korean peninsula. Its place in the calendar was chosen in the week between National Foundation Day on 3 October and Hangeul Day on 9 October.
